paragraphs.title: The Child and His Name: A Sign of Coming Plunder

easy.explanation: The LORD told Isaiah to take a great roll.
easy.q: What did the LORD tell Isaiah to take?

answers: The king of Assyria and the high priest
Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah
easy.explanation: Isaiah named Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah as witnesses.
easy.q: Who were the faithful witnesses Isaiah took?

easy.explanation: The LORD commanded Isaiah to call his son Mahershalalhashbaz.
easy.q: What name was given to Isaiah's son?

answers: To announce that the spoil would come quickly
To describe where the child was born
To remember the names of the witnesses
medium.explanation: The name signified that the spoil would be taken quickly.
medium.q: Why was the name written on the roll and given to the child?

answers: The spoil would soon be taken
The spoil would immediately be returned
medium.explanation: The name announces the swift taking of the spoil.
medium.q: What does “Mahershalalhashbaz” signify in this passage?

answers: Damascus and Samaria would be rebuilt
The riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria would be taken
medium.explanation: The spoil would be taken before the child could call for his parents.
medium.q: What would happen before the child could cry, “My father, and my mother”?

answers: Both were signs of an approaching event
The roll canceled the meaning of the child's birth
The child was named after one of the witnesses
challenge.explanation: Both the inscription and the child's name announced the coming spoil.
challenge.q: What connection is there between the written roll and the birth of the child?

answers: The child was born, then the roll was written, and finally witnesses were chosen
The roll was written, witnesses were taken, and then the child was born
Witnesses were chosen, Damascus was conquered, and then the roll was written
challenge.explanation: The roll was written first, witnesses were named, and afterward the child was born.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the events?

challenge.explanation: The verse says they would be taken before the king of Assyria.
challenge.q: Before whom would the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria be taken?

paragraphs.title: The Waters of Shiloah and the River

answers: The waters of Shiloah that go softly
easy.explanation: The people refused the waters of Shiloah that went softly.
The LORD would bring the king of Assyria like the waters of a mighty river.
easy.q: Whom would the LORD bring upon the land?

easy.explanation: The waters would reach even to the neck.
easy.q: How far would the overflowing waters reach in Judah?

medium.explanation: The softly flowing waters suggest gentleness and moderation.
medium.q: What do the waters of Shiloah represent in the passage?

answers: Because the people rejoiced in Rezin and Remaliah's son
medium.explanation: The people rejected Shiloah and rejoiced in Rezin and Remaliah's son.
medium.q: Why would the mighty river come upon the land?

medium.explanation: The image describes the river's broad spread across the land.
medium.q: What does the river's “wings” filling the land suggest?

answers: Quiet, gentle waters versus a mighty overflowing river
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts softly flowing Shiloah with the strong and overflowing river.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in the description of the waters?

challenge.explanation: Even in the warning, the land is addressed as Immanuel.
challenge.q: What remains within the warning about Judah's distress?

answers: It remains at the border of Damascus
It rises over all its channels and goes over all its banks
It reaches only the waters of Shiloah
challenge.explanation: These words emphasize the river's great strength and spread.
challenge.q: How is the extent of the river's destruction described?

paragraphs.title: The Threat to the Nations and the Security of Immanuel

answers: To the witnesses of the roll
easy.explanation: The command is addressed to the peoples and nations.
easy.q: To whom is the command “Associate yourselves, O ye people” addressed?

easy.explanation: The passage says their counsel would come to nought.
easy.q: What would happen to the counsel of the nations?

answers: Because the land was far away
easy.explanation: The verse ends with the reason: God is with us.
easy.q: Why would the nations' words not stand?

answers: The nations would prepare themselves but still be broken
medium.explanation: The repetition shows that their preparation would not prevent their defeat.
medium.q: What does the repeated command to gird yourselves emphasize?

answers: Both the counsel and the word would fail
The counsel would succeed but the speech would fail
The speech would succeed but the counsel would fail
medium.explanation: Neither their plans nor their words would stand.
medium.q: What relationship does the passage show between counsel and speech?

answers: You will be defeated and shattered
medium.explanation: The phrase describes defeat and ruin.
medium.q: What does “ye shall be broken in pieces” mean in this context?

answers: They are called to strengthen themselves, but they are broken
They are called to flee, but they win
They are called to be silent, but they make a covenant
challenge.explanation: Their attempts to prepare themselves end in defeat.
challenge.q: What is the contrast between the nations' command and its result?

answers: The presence of God with His people
The strength of the city walls
challenge.explanation: Security rests on the declaration, “God is with us.”
challenge.q: What is the basis of the security described in these verses?

answers: It emphasizes the certainty of failure
It marks a change of location
It describes the building of an army
challenge.explanation: The repetition strongly emphasizes the nations' certain defeat.
challenge.q: How does the repetition of “ye shall be broken in pieces” affect the meaning?

paragraphs.title: Fear of God Instead of Political Involvement

answers: The way of the king of Assyria
The way of the waters of Shiloah
easy.explanation: The LORD instructed Isaiah not to walk in the way of the people.
easy.q: What way was Isaiah warned not to follow?

easy.explanation: Isaiah was told to sanctify the LORD of hosts.
easy.q: Whom was Isaiah told to sanctify?

answers: A sanctuary and also a stone of stumbling and a snare
easy.explanation: The LORD would be a sanctuary to some and a stumbling stone and snare to others.
easy.q: What would the LORD be to many people?

answers: Do not allow the people's fears to control or terrify you
Do not write upon the roll
medium.explanation: Isaiah was told not to share the fearful dread of the people.
medium.q: What does “neither fear ye their fear” mean in context?

answers: Sanctify the LORD and regard Him as your fear
medium.explanation: The LORD was to be set apart and regarded with reverence.
medium.q: What should be done instead of following the people's way?

answers: Different people would respond to Him in different ways
He was located in two places
He was described as a river
medium.explanation: He would protect those who trusted Him but become a stumbling stone to others.
medium.q: Why could the LORD be both a sanctuary and a stumbling stone?

answers: Fear of the LORD directs a person, while fear of the people must not rule him
Fear of the LORD means fearing a king, while fear of the people means faith
There is no difference between them
challenge.explanation: Isaiah was to reverence the LORD rather than be controlled by public fear.
challenge.q: What is the contrast between fearing the LORD and fearing the people?

answers: To both the houses of Israel and the inhabitants of Jerusalem
Only to the king of Assyria
Only to the witnesses of the roll
challenge.explanation: The verse names both houses of Israel and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
challenge.q: To whom would the LORD be a stone of stumbling and a snare?

answers: They would stumble, fall, be broken, be snared, and be taken
They would write a new testimony
challenge.explanation: The verse lists a sequence of stumbling, falling, breaking, entrapment, and capture.
challenge.q: What result is described for many of them?

paragraphs.title: The Testimony, the Children, and the Rejection of Mediums

easy.explanation: Isaiah was told to bind up the testimony and seal the law.
easy.q: What was Isaiah told to bind and seal?

easy.explanation: Isaiah declared that he would wait upon the LORD.

answers: Isaiah and the children whom the LORD gave him
easy.explanation: Isaiah and his children were signs and wonders in Israel.
easy.q: Who were given as signs and wonders?

answers: In the palace of the king of Assyria
medium.explanation: The law was to be sealed among the disciples.
medium.q: Where was the law to be sealed?

answers: Going to the king of Assyria
medium.explanation: They suggested seeking those with familiar spirits and wizards that peep and mutter.
medium.q: What did some people suggest doing when they sought an answer?

answers: Their words offer no true light or guidance
The event would happen at sunrise
medium.explanation: The phrase means that their message lacks true light and guidance.
medium.q: What does “there is no light in them” indicate?

answers: Instead of seeking the dead, people should seek their God
Instead of seeking God, people should seek the dead
The passage gives no preference between them
challenge.explanation: Isaiah asks whether a people should not seek unto their God rather than the dead.
challenge.q: What contrast does Isaiah make concerning mediums and the proper source of answers?

answers: They are signs and wonders in Israel
They are witnesses only for the king of Assyria
challenge.explanation: They serve as signs and wonders from the LORD of hosts.
challenge.q: How are Isaiah and his children connected with the prophetic mission?

answers: He seals the testimony, waits upon the LORD, and rejects mediums
He consults mediums, seals the testimony, and rejects the LORD
He abandons the law and seeks the king of Assyria
challenge.explanation: The passage presents Isaiah sealing the word, waiting on the LORD, and rejecting occult guidance.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence of Isaiah's actions in this passage?

paragraphs.title: The Land in Darkness and Distress

easy.explanation: The passage describes the people as hungry.
easy.q: What condition does the person in the land experience?

easy.explanation: He curses his king and his God.
easy.q: Whom does the hungry and angry person curse?

easy.explanation: He sees trouble, darkness, and dimness of anguish.
easy.q: How is the land described when he looks upon it?

medium.explanation: After becoming hungry and angry, he looks upward.
medium.q: What causes the person to look upward?

answers: A condition of distress and oppression
A quick journey to the river
medium.explanation: The phrase belongs to the passage's description of trouble and distress.
The passage mentions the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali.
medium.q: Which places are mentioned as being affected first and later?

answers: Distress leads people to seek answers, but the search does not resolve it
The distress has no connection with the search
challenge.explanation: The suffering prompts a search for guidance, but turning to mediums leaves the darkness unresolved.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the distress and the search for mediums?

answers: From hunger to anger, cursing, and a search for answers
From joy to fear and victory
From faith to peace and abundance
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from hunger to anger and cursing, followed by a troubled search.

answers: The distress spreads and becomes more severe
The land is freed from its enemy
The threat is reduced to Damascus alone
challenge.explanation: The description shows increasing trouble and darkness across the land.
challenge.q: What does the movement from the earlier condition to the final darkness suggest?
